newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN BANKS' Q3 PROFIT IN LINE WITH Q2 - BFC.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN BANKS' Q3 PROFIT IN LINE WITH Q2 - BFC.

text.p: Third-quarter profits of the Belgian banking sector should be similar to the relatively weak second quarter, the regulatory Banking and Finance Commission (BFC) said on Thursday.
"Profit evolution in the third quarter should be in line with that of the second quarter," said BFC director Marcel Maes at the presentation of the regulator's 1995/96 annual report.
He said that the second quarter had been weaker than the first quarter, and declined to give an outlook for the second half of 1996.
In the first half of 1996, Belgian banks earned a total profit of 33.38 billion francs, up 23 percent compared to the weak first half of 1995.
"The strong first-half earnings rise was due mainly to the first quarter," the BFC said in a statement.

The BFC also said that in the first nine months of 1996 the sector's balance sheet total increased by nearly 10 percent to more than 27,000 billion francs. The balance sheet total of the seven biggest banks rose 14 percent to 17,800 billion.
In the first nine months of 1996 client deposits rose by 6.5 percent to 12,800 billion and credits to clients by seven percent to nearly 8,900 billion.
